title: restoreVersion can restore a commit from another document

evidence.quote: const doc = this.getDocument(documentId); const source = this.getCommit(commitId); ... this.insertCommit(doc.id, branch.id, ... source.modelHash ...)
if (from.documentId !== doc.id) throw new Error('Cannot branch from another document');
const result = this.store.restoreVersion(documentId, commitId); if (result.created) { this.writeFileFromCommit(documentId, result.commit.id); }
restore re-commits old content onto the current branch reusing objects

reasoning: restoreVersion accepts a documentId and a commitId but never checks that the source commit belongs to that document. A wrong or stale UI/IPC call can create a commit on document A containing document B's model/file hashes, and the desktop service then writes those bytes to document A's path. createBranch already has the analogous cross-document guard, which makes restoreVersion inconsistent with the store's own safety model.
reproduction: Commit document A and document B, then call restoreVersion(A.id, commitFromB.id). The method creates a new commit on A's current branch with B's hashes; DocumentService.restoreVersion would then overwrite A's file on disk with B's bytes.
recommendation: Add `if (source.documentId !== doc.id) throw new Error('Cannot restore a version from another document')` before reading the current branch or inserting the restore commit.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing restore test only restores a commit from the same document and does not exercise mismatched documentId/commitId inputs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with two tracked documents asserting restoreVersion(documentA.id, documentBCommit.id) throws and leaves document A's branch head unchanged.
minimumFixScope: SnapshotStore.restoreVersion validation plus a cross-document restore regression test.
